annotations.annotation_text: Counting in Irish (aon, dó, trí), establishing the pedagogical and numerical themes of the Night Lessons while linking back to the tripartite structure.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Establishes the thematic link between the children's ravenous consumption of knowledge and physical eating, merging intellect and appetite.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Theological undertones of the Eucharist (eating the god/father), framed through the savage lens of tribal survival and filial usurpation.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Elevates the brute act of consumption into a ritualistic communion, foreshadowing the collective ingestion of HCE's mythic body.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The seventh thunder-word (100 letters). It synthesizes themes of choral singing, drumming, the fall of Humpty Dumpty, and agricultural harvest, representing the noise of gluttonous consumption.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Reference to the medieval university curriculum (arithmetic, geometry, music, astronomy), anchoring the children's study in scholastic tradition.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The lower division of the liberal arts (grammar, logic, rhetoric), representing the foundational linguistic play that Joyce subverts.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: The physical act that unifies the consumption of food, words, and the father-figure in the nocturnal classroom setting.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. http://fweet.org
